races.name: Kauto The King Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Hercule Du Seuil
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces tactical disadvantage with soft pace but Harry Cobden brings strong Newton Abbot form to this assignment
runners_data.comment: Grade 3 winner (2m4f) for Willie Mullins last year but offered little as yet for new yard.
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to make an impact in three starts for this yard this year, but he showed some smart form in Ireland for Willie Mullins, notably landing a 2m4f Grade 3 at around this time last season; looks attractively treated on that evidence; one to watch in the market, though a return to form is needed.

runners_data.name: Etalon
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with class edge but 74 days off and cheekpieces fitted suggest Dan Skelton expects improvement needed
runners_data.comment: Ascot win and good third since the cheekpieces went on; below par latest but respected.
runners_data.spotlight: Fitting of cheekpieces sparked a revival in December, when landing a fifth success over fences at Ascot (2m3f, good to soft); followed that up with a career-best RPR when third off this mark there (2m5f) the following month; respected but he'll need to leave behind a lesser effort last time.

runners_data.name: Light N Strike
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits if pace develops but 193 days absence and stable switch creates significant question marks
runners_data.comment: Won this off today's mark last year but form for this stable has been poor.
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive for Emma Lavelle last term, winning this off today's mark and backing it up with solid placed efforts; however, he's struggled for this yard (early unseat in Kerry National, pulled up at Chepstow and tailed off at Cheltenham when last seen in October) and now has something to prove.

runners_data.name: Centara
runners_data.note: Front runner perfectly positioned to control race but 194-day layoff after disappointing Punchestown effort raises fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Five chase wins last summer; second wind op; steps up in trip but needs to find more.
runners_data.spotlight: Highly progressive over fences last summer, winning five handicaps (four here) at around 2m on ground no worse than good to soft, though he ended the campaign pulled up at Cheltenham; has since had a second wind op and could find more at this longer trip (2m3f hurdle winner), which will be needed off this mark following a break.

runners_data.name: Western General
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with ideal tactical setup and solid recent Chepstow/Hereford form gives him strong winning claims
runners_data.comment: Back to form post wind op; up in trip but respected judged on recent good form.
runners_data.spotlight: Back to form after a second wind op, posting career-best RPRs when scoring at Chepstow in February and when runner-up at Hereford the following month (both at 2m); has his best form over shorter but shapes as though this trip should suit and he commands respect on that recent form.

runners_data.name: Ventura Highway
runners_data.note: Prominent style helps but French form hard to translate and 148 days since last meaningful effort creates uncertainty
runners_data.comment: Ex-French; Auteuil winner last May; below par since; bit to prove on UK debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French; gained a chase success at Auteuil (2m6f) last May but hasn't matched that since; current ability is a little tricky to pin down and he looks to have something to find on RPRs on this British debut.

runners_data.name: Somespring Special
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner facing tactical disadvantage but 24-day break keeps her sharp and previous Chepstow win shows ability
runners_data.comment: 4-15 over fences; below par twice this year; only 2lb lower and has something to prove.
runners_data.spotlight: 4-15 over fences; gained a win at Chepstow (extended 2m3f, good) in October but hit with a 7lb rise and she's been well held on both outings this year, most recently trailing home last of three at Wincanton (2m, good) three weeks ago; only 2lb lower and now has plenty to prove.

races.paceDynamic: Centara is the only confirmed front runner in this seven-horse field and should be allowed to dictate terms from the start without pressure. Western General and Ventura Highway as prominent racers will sit within striking distance but won't challenge for the lead early. The lack of genuine pace-setters means Centara can control fractions over the 2m5f trip, setting up a tactical affair where the hold-up horses (Hercule Du Seuil, Etalon, Light N Strike, Somespring Special) will need to rely on finishing kicks. This race shape strongly favours the front runner and prominent racers who can secure good positions without expending energy early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Centara Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Centara maintains his usual front-running style without pressure from the field
scenarios.body: The Paul Nicholls runner can dictate conservative fractions and kick clear approaching the last, with Western General best placed to follow him through. Both horses avoid the traffic problems that will plague the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Rally
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish from the back straight
scenarios.body: The class horses Hercule Du Seuil and Etalon can unleash their superior finishing speed despite poor positioning early. Harry Cobden and Harry Skelton will need to thread their mounts through traffic but have the pace to reel in the leaders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Positioning Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Western General and Ventura Highway press forward to challenge Centara for the lead
scenarios.body: The increased pace will set up the race for a closer who can stay on strongly, with Etalon's proven class and Harry Skelton's tactical nous coming to the fore. Light N Strike could benefit as the forgotten horse with legitimate claims off his current mark.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Centara goes too slow and the field bunches up turning for home
scenarios.body: A cavalry charge develops where track position and luck in running become crucial, potentially favouring Somespring Special who can quicken despite her recent poor form. Western General's prominent style gives him the best chance to avoid trouble.

watchPoints.text: Centara may not handle the soft ground despite past good to soft form - any early signs of struggling could collapse the pace scenario
Western General and Ventura Highway might press forward more aggressively than expected, creating genuine pace pressure on Centara
Hercule Du Seuil and Etalon both returning from long breaks - watch for signs of ring-rustiness in the early stages
Light N Strike making stable debut for Mickey Bowen after 193 days off - market support would be significant given the circumstances
Somespring Special's recent poor form masks her October Chepstow win - any confident riding from Ben Jones could signal a return to form

races.name: Racing To School Reaches 25 Years Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Bold Step
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with Henderson's 117-day break expertise, proven on similar going and distance suited

runners_data.name: Outmaster
runners_data.note: Lightly raced Nicholls runner with unknown stamina reserves, 388-day absence a major concern

runners_data.name: River Don
runners_data.note: Point winner with cheekpieces added, stamina proven but amateur jockey claim a potential negative
runners_data.comment: Off mark at seventh attempt in points last month; cheekpieces on for rules/hurdle debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the seventh attempt in points when winning a three-finisher maiden at Cothelstone (3m, good to soft) last month for this stable; cheekpieces go on for rules/hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: Jubertilee
runners_data.note: Faded badly on rules debut at shorter trip, stamina doubts despite point form
runners_data.comment: 6-21 in points; well held Chepstow debut over 2m but this longer trip will suit.
runners_data.spotlight: 6-21 in points and in good heart this year, but never sighted when well held on hurdle/rules debut at Chepstow last month, possibly finding the drop to 2m counting against him; should be better suited by this stamina test but still likely to find a few too good.

runners_data.name: Name Me Nicely
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse needing strong pace, solid recent form but poor strike rate on similar going

runners_data.name: At Sunrise
runners_data.note: Natural leader returning from 147-day break, headgear applied suggests connections expect improvement

runners_data.name: Lirone Du Seuil
runners_data.note: French winner who disappointed on British debut, needs to prove stamina at this trip
runners_data.comment: Bit to prove returning from a break, but tongue-tie added and remains in excellent hands.
runners_data.spotlight: French 2m2f hurdle winner on very soft who folded tamely at Wetherby (2m, soft; 14-1) on British debut, and fared little better when a remote fourth at Plumpton (2m4f, soft) in January; has a bit to prove returning from a break but now goes in a tongue-tie and remains in excellent hands.

runners_data.name: Alberts Bay
runners_data.note: Front runner with huge absence concerns, shown ability over course and distance previously
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 9yo; career hit by absences; back after another break on this stable debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Third on hurdle debut over C&D in September 2023 after a long absence, but off again afterwards and last of seven in October 2024; returns from another lengthy layoff on stable debut.

runners_data.name: Double Tiger
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with good recent form, proven stamina and reliable jumping

runners_data.name: Style De Folie
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with poor recent form, cheekpieces applied but hard to fancy on evidence
runners_data.comment: Well held in both hurdle starts (2m3f); cheekpieces latest; up in trip but hard to fancy.
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 53l and 31l in his two hurdle races (2m3f), with cheekpieces latest; up in trip but difficult to make a case for.

races.paceDynamic: At Sunrise and Alberts Bay will contest the early lead, with both confirmed front runners likely to set a solid gallop over this staying trip on soft ground. Bold Step and Double Tiger should track prominently behind the leaders, while the hold-up horses Name Me Nicely, Lirone Du Seuil and Style De Folie will need the pace to collapse to get competitive. The combination of two keen leaders and testing conditions should create a strong pace that will find out the stamina reserves. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those with proven stamina, as the likely strong gallop will stretch the field and expose any lack of staying power in the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Prominents
scenarios.trigger: If At Sunrise and Alberts Bay duel from the start creating a searching gallop
scenarios.body: The honest pace plays into the hands of those tracking just behind, allowing them to strike when the leaders weaken in the final half-mile. Bold Step and Double Tiger are perfectly positioned to capitalize when the front pair tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leaders Dominate Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If At Sunrise finds his best form and gets an uncontested lead
scenarios.body: The front runner can dictate terms and kick clear when the field comes under pressure, with any chasing pack struggling to reel him in on the testing ground. At Sunrise's stamina credentials shine through despite his long absence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses and becomes pedestrian
scenarios.body: Name Me Nicely and Lirone Du Seuil can use their class advantage to sweep past a tiring field in the final furlong. The lack of early pace allows the hold-up horses to conserve energy for a devastating late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart with multiple fallers or a messy pace
scenarios.body: The lightly raced improvers like Outmaster and River Don can capitalize on a muddling race where class tells less than stamina and jumping. Paul Nicholls' Outmaster particularly appeals if getting a soft lead to aim at.

watchPoints.text: Alberts Bay's fitness after 573-day layoff could see him fold quickly if forced to make the running
Name Me Nicely needs a strong pace to be effective but may get outpaced if the tempo becomes frantic
Watch Outmaster's jumping early as any mistakes will end hopes for the lightly raced Nicholls runner
At Sunrise's headgear first-time suggests ability but 147-day break makes fitness a question mark
River Don's amateur rider could prove costly if precise jumping is required in the home straight

races.name: No Drama This End Club Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Elysian Knight
runners_data.note: Front-running style suits but 0-4 over fences this term suggests current ability questioned despite recent hurdles fourth
runners_data.comment: Yet to win over fences or in handicap company but needs respect dropped into a class 4.
runners_data.spotlight: 0-4 over fences this term but far from disgraced on a couple of starts and ran respectably when fourth back over hurdles at Plumpton (3m1f, good) last month; yet to win in handicap company but drops in class returned to fences and warrants respect.

runners_data.name: Storminhome
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with Harry Skelton's tactical brilliance and blinkers boost from narrow Southwell second creates winning chance
runners_data.comment: Back to form in blinkers latest and likely to play a leading role if headgear works again.
runners_data.spotlight: Suffered a couple of heavy defeats after a long absence but then went very close to a first chase win in first-time blinkers at Southwell (3m, soft) last time, with the winner running well since; remains on a competitive mark and is one to consider if the headgear continues to have a positive effect.

runners_data.name: Astronomic View
runners_data.note: Proven on similar going with solid recent chase form but Sue Gardner's minimal strike-rate raises training concerns

runners_data.name: Rickety Bridge
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls angle interesting but largely out of form since 2024 hurdles win and needs significant revival
runners_data.comment: Signs of a revival last time and he could be suited by switch to fences.
runners_data.spotlight: Landed a Southwell maiden hurdle (2m4f, soft) in March 2024; largely out of form in limited starts since but there were signs of a revival here (3m2f, good) last month in first-time cheekpieces; needs to back that up but could improve for this switch to fences.

runners_data.name: Dyno Dave
runners_data.note: Henderson stable form decent but unseat last time and 29 days off creates fitness questions despite previous chase win

races.paceDynamic: With all five runners carrying prominent/front-running styles, this will be a genuine battle for the early lead between Elysian Knight, Storminhome, and Astronomic View. The pace will be honest from the outset over this stamina-sapping 3m2f trip on soft ground, with no confirmed hold-up horses to allow any breathers. The sustained gallop will create a true test of stamina where tactical positioning matters less than pure staying power. This race shape strongly favours the most genuine stayers who can maintain their gallop to the line, penalising horses dependent on tactical pace changes.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Genuine Staying Test
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest throughout with multiple leaders
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop becomes a war of attrition where only the truest stayers survive. Horses with proven stamina reserves and recent form over extended trips will prevail when others weaken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too hard early and capitulate
scenarios.body: The aggressive early pace backfires as leaders tie up, allowing the best-balanced horse to inherit. Fresh legs and tactical awareness from the jockey become crucial factors.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Skelton Tactical Masterclass
scenarios.trigger: If Harry Skelton times Storminhome's challenge perfectly
scenarios.body: The champion jockey uses his mount's class and recent blinkers improvement to devastating effect. Storminhome's near-miss last time translates to breakthrough victory under patient riding.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Nicholls Revival Special
scenarios.trigger: If Rickety Bridge shows dramatic improvement from his yard
scenarios.body: The master trainer's ability to rejuvenate horses produces a surprise performance. The Henderson-trained runner's proven class emerges despite recent poor form.

watchPoints.text: Storminhome with Harry Skelton could time his challenge perfectly if the pace is strong early
Elysian Knight's jumping under pressure given his recent fence struggles this season
Astronomic View's stamina reserves in the final furlong given his mixed recent finishing efforts
Rickety Bridge for any market confidence given Paul Nicholls' ability to improve horses dramatically
Early pace battle between the front three which could set up the race for a closer or strong traveller

races.name: Welcoming Newton Abbot Business Club Members Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Northern Air
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 32-day break with an inconsistent recent record, needs strong pace to be effective but unlikely to get it here.

runners_data.name: First Angel
runners_data.note: Prominent racer ideally positioned for this race shape, though the 50-day absence and age concerns at 10 years old are potential negatives.

runners_data.name: Cobbler's Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer from the powerful Skelton yard but his disappointing recent chase form suggests he's still finding his feet over fences.
runners_data.comment: Good-ground hurdle winner; yet to win over fences but latest fourth was encouraging.
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground 2m maiden hurdle winner a year ago and he's looked a work in progress since switching to fences last season; latest 5l fourth at Ascot (2m1f, good) returned to better ground was encouraging though and he's come a long way down the weights; needs to build on that and not of of this if doing so.

runners_data.name: Lightning Flash
runners_data.note: Showed promise when winning on chase debut but the fall last time creates questions about confidence, though prominent style suits this race.
runners_data.comment: Won chase debut at Chepstow but out of form since falling at Ludlow in November.
runners_data.spotlight: Made a winning start over fences at Chepstow (2m) in October and looked set for a second success when falling two out at Ludlow (2m) the following month; however, well held in his two runs since, with his jumping far from fluent when last of three at Doncaster in March after a break; now has something to prove.

runners_data.name: Gower Prince
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who can control this race from the front, recent second at Market Rasen with hood reapplied suggests return to form.
runners_data.comment: Back to near best when second on stable debut last time and strong claims if repeating it.
runners_data.spotlight: Back to near best on first start for this stable when runner-up at Market Rasen (2m1f, good) with the hood back on; remains well treated on past form after 3lb rise and holds strong claims if able to repeat the effort.

races.paceDynamic: Gower Prince will dictate from the front with no other confirmed pace-setters in this small field, likely creating a moderate tempo over the first half of this 2m½f trip. First Angel and Lightning Flash will track prominently behind the leader, while Northern Air and Cobbler's Boy will settle further back as hold-up horses. With only one natural front-runner and no early pace pressure, Gower Prince can control the gallop and save energy for the finish. This race shape clearly favours the prominent racers who can position close enough to strike when the pace inevitably quickens, as the hold-up horses may find insufficient pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Power Play
scenarios.trigger: If First Angel or Lightning Flash can track Gower Prince at comfortable fractions and stay in touch turning for home.
scenarios.body: The moderate early pace allows the prominent runners to conserve energy while staying close enough to pounce when the race develops in earnest. Both have the class and tactical speed to exploit this positioning advantage over horses coming from further back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Gower Prince Wire Job
scenarios.trigger: If Gower Prince can dictate his ideal fractions and find enough in reserve when challenged in the straight.
scenarios.body: The uncontested lead allows him to save energy early and his recent Market Rasen second suggests he's back to form with the hood back on. The lack of early pace pressure plays directly into his tactical preference for controlling races.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly dawdling and Northern Air or Cobbler's Boy get the strong gallop they need from the back.
scenarios.body: The hold-up pair would benefit from a truly-run race where they can unleash their finishing kicks, but the likely lack of early pace works against their preferred racing pattern. Both need others to create the tempo they require to be effective.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Gower Prince stops quickly in front and the race becomes a sprint from the final fence.
scenarios.body: The entire complexion changes if the leader empties out, turning it into a dash where any horse with a turn of foot can capitalise regardless of early position. This scenario levels the playing field but seems unlikely given recent form evidence.

watchPoints.text: Lightning Flash must prove the Ludlow fall hasn't affected his jumping confidence, especially at the business end of the race.
Gower Prince's stamina for this trip on testing ground after his recent layoff, particularly if forced to go faster than ideal early.
Northern Air's fitness levels after 32 days off and whether Tom Broughton can get him into contention from his hold-up style.
First Angel's ability to handle the step up in class after his long break, given his advancing years at 10.
Cobbler's Boy's jumping under pressure if he gets competitive, given his recent struggles to complete over fences.

races.name: Par Inn Celebrating 50 Next Year Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ghost Dancing
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid form figures who should appreciate the strong pace and testing ground combination.

runners_data.name: Belle Le Grand
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner coming back from a break with top weight but has won over this C&D previously.
runners_data.comment: 0-5 in handicaps but she's on a reduced mark and could be dangerous with cheekpieces added
runners_data.spotlight: Won two novice hurdles on good ground last May (2m/2m1f); no impact at 12-1 or bigger in five handicaps but she rallied to finish a respectable sixth of 15 at Kelso (2m, good to soft) in March; continues to drop down the weights and could be dangerous if first-time cheekpieces work.

runners_data.name: Future Bucks
runners_data.note: Keen front-runner who was pulled up last time, raising questions about her attitude to racing.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up on handicap debut at Newbury in March and needs a major revival back in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French 5yo who won British debut at Windsor (2m, good to soft) in November but she's been disappointing since and was pulled on handicap debut at Newbury (2m4f, good to soft; 66-1) in March; that was a tough assignment but she needs a major revival on this drop back in trip.

runners_data.name: Riviera Walk
runners_data.note: Another pace-setter with an inexperienced 5lb claimer aboard, adding pressure in a competitive pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Easy winner of a Catterick maiden but was pulled up on her handicap debut last time
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper scorer who won by 15l in a Catterick maiden (1m7f, good) in March but she was pulled up on her handicap debut at Kelso (2m, good to soft) last time; still has low mileage but she's not been easy to predict and needs to bounce back again.

runners_data.name: Best Night
runners_data.note: Versatile prominent racer who acts on the ground and has recent C&D winning form to recommend her.
runners_data.comment: Won at Huntingdon (2m, good) in March but she's taken two backward steps since
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on good and soft ground; C&D winner who scored at Huntingdon (2m) in March but she's taken backward steps in her two subsequent runs; only 2lb higher than for her last win but she needs to rediscover her spark.

runners_data.name: Babychino
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who showed improved form when third at long odds last time but faces a tactical disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Third on handicap debut at Uttoxeter but she's 5lb out of the weights here; has work to do
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo; came from long way back to finish third on handicap debut at Uttoxeter (2m, good to soft; 50-1) in March but she was beaten 11l and this is tougher from 5lb out of the weights; has work to do.

runners_data.name: Miss Denver
runners_data.note: Prominent type but spotlight comment warns she fades in the finish, problematic in a staying test.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed 6yo and she's a possible improver on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to three hurdle winners including the smart Polly Peachum (2m-2m6f); well held at big prices in both completed starts over hurdles but she's had only four runs and it wouldn't be a surprise if she showed a lot more on this handicap debut; needs a close look in the market.

runners_data.name: Reel Orange
runners_data.note: Recent C&D winner from hold-up style but will need the pace to collapse to be competitive from her usual position.
runners_data.comment: Made the breakthrough over C&D last month and she's a big player again off 3lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the ninth attempt over hurdles when justifying favouritism in a C&D handicap (good; cheekpieces added) last month; there wasn't much separating the first four but a 3lb rise looks fair and her confidence should be boosted after that success; big player again in her bid to make it 2-4 for Joe Tizzard.

races.paceDynamic: Riviera Walk, Belle Le Grand, and Future Bucks will ensure a strong early gallop with all three natural front-runners unwilling to give ground. The pace will be honest throughout the 2m1f trip on testing ground, with the leaders likely stringing out the field early. Any that get detached from the main group will struggle to make up ground in the conditions. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those with proven stamina reserves who can track the pace and pounce late, penalising hold-up horses who rely on a finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners go too fast early and tie up in the soft ground.
scenarios.body: The leaders will weaken significantly in the final half-mile, allowing patient types to pick up the pieces. Hold-up horses like Babychino and Reel Orange benefit from the pace meltdown despite the tactical disadvantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Test
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but sustainable, creating a true staying test.
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will find out the stamina-shy and favour those with proven endurance over the trip. Best Night and Ghost Dancing can track the pace and have the engine to sustain their effort to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders gets first run and the pace is more measured than expected.
scenarios.body: The early leader will have enough left to resist late challengers on ground that makes closing difficult. Belle Le Grand or Future Bucks could dominate from the front with their class edge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders hesitate early, creating a stop-start pace.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where horse with the best turn of foot prevails regardless of usual tactics. Ghost Dancing's class could tell in a messy tactical affair.

watchPoints.text: Future Bucks was pulled up on her last start and if she shows similar reluctance early, it removes a key pace angle.
Watch Riviera Walk's inexperienced 5lb claimer Benjamin Macey in the early pace battle against seasoned professionals.
Best Night ran just 14 days ago and this quick turnaround could either have her spot-on or leave her vulnerable late.
Belle Le Grand carries top weight of 168lbs and hasn't won since May, making her task tough despite her natural pace advantage.
The soft ground could play more testing than expected given Newton Abbot's current good to soft official going.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Juggernaut
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who stayed on well over 3m2f at Stratford last time, Honeyball's strong recent form adds appeal
runners_data.comment: Reliable type who was a good second when upped to 3m2f at Stratford last time; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Reliable type who has finished runner-up at Fontwell (2m1f, good) and Stratford (3m2f, good) this spring; that was his first run beyond 2m5f last time but he stayed on well and is respected off an unchanged mark.

runners_data.name: Striking A Pose
runners_data.note: Made all to win here three weeks ago, 10-year-old veteran knows how to dictate from the front
runners_data.comment: Six-time hurdle winner who made all over C&D last month; big player again back up 4lb
runners_data.spotlight: Recorded his sixth hurdle win when making all off a reduced mark over C&D (good; 4-1) three weeks ago; back up 4lb but remains well treated on old form and is versatile ground-wise; key player.

runners_data.name: Baltray
runners_data.note: Prominent type struggling for form, hasn't won a hurdle since 2022 despite regular placing
runners_data.comment: Has struggled in his last two starts and has stamina to prove at this new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up off 3lb higher at Stratford (2m6f, good) in October but he's struggled in both subsequent runs; hurdling record is now 1-10 and he has stamina to prove at this new trip after another break; down the list.

runners_data.name: Mister Barclay
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with class edge, 178 days off but excellent soft ground record and claims assistance

runners_data.name: Supreme Yeats
runners_data.note: Hold-up type well handicapped on old form but 0-9 since July win, Skelton stable firing
runners_data.comment: On dangerous mark but he's been out of sorts this year and losing run is mounting up
runners_data.spotlight: Well handicapped on his Uttoxeter win (3m, good) last July but he's 0-9 since and has been out of sorts this year; has something to prove and he was pulled up in only go at this sort of trip; cheekpieces (last used in October) are reapplied.

runners_data.name: Alan Bresil
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up horse who handles soft ground, trainer out of form but trip should suit

runners_data.name: Despereaux

runners_data.spotlight: Conditions are no problem but he's not won since July 2024 and has struggled in both runs this year, including on stable debut at Ffos Las (ran in snatches) last month; has plenty to prove and needs to get back on track.

races.paceDynamic: Striking A Pose will dictate from the front having won making all here three weeks ago, with Juggernaut, Baltray and Despereaux settling prominently behind him. The sustainable gallop will allow hold-up horses Mister Barclay, Supreme Yeats and I Am Spider Man to get into contention turning for home. Over this extended 3m2½f trip on soft ground, stamina becomes paramount and the genuine pace will set up perfectly for closers. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can stay the trip and finish powerfully.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuine but not overly strong
scenarios.body: The stamina test exposes the prominent racers in the final half-mile while the hold-up brigade arrive with late surges. Mister Barclay's class and Supreme Yeats' Skelton polish prove decisive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sustains
scenarios.trigger: If Striking A Pose gets an easy lead and dictates throughout
scenarios.body: The 10-year-old uses his course experience to control the tempo and kicks clear before the closers can mount their challenges. His reduced weight and winning form here prove crucial.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses early and becomes stop-start
scenarios.body: Juggernaut benefits from his prominent position to strike in the straight when the race comes alive. His recent Stratford second over this trip and Honeyball's form edge carry him home.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground and trip finds out multiple runners
scenarios.body: Several runners fail to see out the extended distance creating a messy finish. The most genuine stayer from those left standing prevails in a weak time.

Mister Barclay fitness after 178-day break, needs to be sharp from the start
